clue.text: Fights over' casserole containing fine sea food

indicators.note: over tells us the word for fights is turned round, read from end to start

parts.note: rows are fights or quarrels

indicators.note: the dish holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a casserole is a cooked dish
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Someone moves on from brawling to a casserole with a fine seafood filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the fights word round to give SWOR. 'Sea food' looks like seafood on a plate, but it is a fish of the sea itself. The stray apostrophe is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The swordfish is a large ocean fish served as seafood, so it is literally a sea food.

clue.text: After second drink, girl's first kissing and cuddling

parts.note: a noggin is a small measure of drink

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word for the girl

explanation.surface: After a quick drink, a girl leads the way into some kissing and cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Snogging is British slang for kissing and cuddling, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Archer's shot head off pigeon

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the bird's name is removed

parts.note: the pouter is a breed of pigeon with an inflatable crop

explanation.surface: An archer's arrow takes the head off a pigeon.
explanation.walkthrough: An outer is the outermost ring of an archery target, or a shot landing there.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery a shot hitting the outer ring of the target is called by that ring's name.

clue.text: Child maybe with extremely delicate piece of jewellery

indicators.note: extremely asks for the letters at the extremes of delicate, its first and last

parts.note: a pendant is a piece of jewellery hung on a chain

explanation.surface: A child, perhaps, given a very delicate pendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is an example of someone who relies on another for support, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Effective, as policemen are

definitions.meaning: a law that is effective is operative, currently applying
police officers belong to the police force, so they are members of it

explanation.definitionFit: A rule in operation is said to be valid now; police officers serve within the constabulary.

clue.text: Help! Tea has been brewed but there's little left to drink

indicators.note: brewed suggests the letters are stirred up and remixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cries for help because the tea is made but barely any remains in the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been brewed' rearranges HELP and TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeltap is the small amount of liquor left at the bottom of a glass.

clue.text: Far from healthy-looking snack

definitions.meaning: a Cornish ... is a pastry turnover eaten as a snack

explanation.definitionFit: A pallid face is described with this adjective; the noun is a filled pastry case eaten on the go.

clue.text: Old man left his wife in Spanish town

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
the old man's wife is the mother, ma

explanation.surface: An old man abandoned his wife in a Spanish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Palma is the capital of Majorca, a Spanish city.

clue.text: Considered holding celebration for an odd number

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: seen can mean considered, as in 'seen as'
an event can be a celebration or occasion

explanation.surface: Thought to be hosting a party for an unusual number of guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is not divisible by two, so it is an odd number.

clue.text: Monarch supporting royal house delivery

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the monarch beneath the house

parts.note: York was an English royal house
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch backs a royal dynasty's delivery of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket ball pitched right at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; this one lands at the batter's toes.

clue.text: Pensioner checks book is readily available

indicators.note: checks here means holds back or contains, so the pensioner surrounds the book

parts.note: OAP stands for old-age pensioner
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A pensioner checks that a book can be borrowed straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on draught from a tap is to hand whenever wanted, an idiom for available.

clue.text: Butcher's gift for glutton?

definitions.meaning: offal handed over for nothing by the meat seller
someone who indulges freely in food and drink

explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats and drinks to excess is called by this term; the question mark flags the punning split.

clue.text: Gather daughter is engaged as actress

indicators.note: is engaged means the daughter is held within the word for gather

parts.note: to garner is to gather or collect

explanation.surface: Someone collects that their daughter has landed an acting job.
explanation.walkthrough: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava Gardner was a famous American screen performer.

clue.text: Apprentice making quality joint, some may say

indicators.note: some may say signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: a trait is a quality or characteristic; the knee is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: An apprentice crafts a good-quality joint, as some would put it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a learner in a trade, a synonym for someone in training.

clue.text: Stand no chance, being graceless?

definitions.meaning: lacking a grace, the short prayer said before a meal

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having no hope; the second reading takes grace literally as a prayer before eating.

clue.text: Blunders encompass course for high-fliers once

indicators.note: encompass means the blunders word surrounds the course word

parts.note: trips are stumbles or blunders
a lane is a course, as in a running track

explanation.surface: Errors surround a track meant for flyers of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Triplanes, with three wings, were early aircraft, so they flew high in former times.

clue.text: A dog keeps quiet for man giving out the post

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: keeps means the dog holds the quiet letter inside it

parts.note: a pointer is a breed of gun dog
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A dog stays silent for the postman.
explanation.walkthrough: The post is a job, not mail: an appointer gives people positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who appoints others assigns them a position, a post.

clue.text: That female doctor frequently going up to town

parts.note: her refers to that female

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means these letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A woman doctor often travels up to town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns DROFT into TFORD. Hertford is the county town of Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hertford is an English town, the seat of its county.

clue.text: Is cooperating, very remarkably, to make cake

indicators.note: remarkably signals the letters are rearranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Being remarkably helpful leads to baking a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges IS COOPERATING plus V. A Victoria sponge is a classic British jam-filled cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria sponge is a layered sponge cake with jam and cream, a specific example.

clue.text: Members of crew only partly tolerating seasickness

indicators.note: only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sailors are only partly able to put up with seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratings are ordinary naval sailors, members of a ship's company.

clue.text: English grub unusual in a European restaurant

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the two letters around them
unusual signals the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: English food tastes strange in a continental eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns E and GRUB into UBERG, which goes 'in' A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn, a place serving food and lodging.

clue.text: We're told to put 'em in a folder for the botany division

indicators.note: we're told signals the spoken sound of the words matters

parts.note: to place them in a folder is to file them

explanation.surface: Instructions to place them in a folder for the plant science department.
explanation.definitionFit: A phylum is a major taxonomic rank, used in classifying plants as a division.

clue.text: Tight, offering only partial share in profits

definitions.text: offering only partial share in profits
definitions.meaning: giving someone fifty per cent of the takings

explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy is a sense of this British slang term; read literally it is a share of only half.

clue.text: Gloat, getting new sporting award

parts.note: to crow is to gloat or boast

explanation.surface: A winner brags on getting a fresh trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown is a title in sport, as in a championship won.

clue.text: Escape trouble during fight

indicators.note: during means the trouble comes in the middle of the fight

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Getting out of a jam in the middle of a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To bail out is to escape, as from an aircraft or a predicament.

clue.text: Gloomy, not having lead in card game

indicators.note: not having lead means the first letter of the word for gloomy is dropped

parts.note: sombre means dark and gloomy

explanation.surface: Downcast at not leading in a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old Spanish trick-taking game played with cards.

clue.text: Man of means having an unhappy experience at length

parts.note: taken as written
a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: A wealthy man has a long spell of bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone owning landed property is traditionally wealthy, a man of means.

clue.text: Drug rings banned

parts.note: a tab is a tablet of a drug
O is ring-shaped, so two rings give OO

explanation.surface: Drug circles are outlawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom, so it is banned.

clue.text: Postgraduate qualifications paid for by member of charitable society

parts.note: MAs are Master of Arts degrees
on, as in 'drinks on me', means paid for by

explanation.surface: Higher degrees funded by someone in a benevolent organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons are a fraternal order noted for charitable work, and a mason is one of them.

clue.text: Take charge of fashion parades in which male takes part

indicators.note: in which says the male goes inside the reshaped letters
to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: Organise catwalk shows where one man takes part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges the parades into SPEARAD, before the male pronoun goes in. 'Fashion parades' reads as catwalk shows, but fashion is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead something is to lead it, taking charge of its front.
